fields.meta_description: Describe how your team sells and get sales automation that routes new leads, follows up after demos and flags stalled deals. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Sales Automation for Every Lead, Deal and Renewal
fields.hero_description: Describe how leads reach your team and when a deal needs a nudge. Emergent builds the routing, follow-ups and renewal alerts on top of your CRM, as code you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sales Automation Handles for Reps
fields.features_subheading: Sales automation hands the repeat steps of a deal to software. Each of these six runs on a rule your team writes.
fields.feature_1:
Every new lead assigned on arrival

Demo requests, chat leads and event scans land in one table. Each new lead goes to a rep by territory or by round-robin rotation. The queue shows whose turn is next.
fields.feature_2:
Sequences sent from each rep's own inbox

Emails go out from the rep's own Gmail or Outlook, in their name, on the days the team picks. Reps can see which step each prospect is on before they pick up the phone.
fields.feature_3:
Activity written back to the CRM

Sent emails and meeting notes sync to Salesforce or HubSpot through their APIs. Each contact record shows its latest touch without a rep typing it in on Friday afternoon.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts on deals that slip

A close date pushed twice, or a proposal with no answer after a week, sends the owner a Slack message. It comes back each morning until someone moves the deal forward.
fields.feature_5:
Discount approvals in Slack

A discount above the threshold goes to a sales manager in Slack. The request shows deal size and margin. Each decision is logged on the opportunity under the approver's name.
fields.feature_6:
Territory rules your engineers can read

Routing tables, cadences and the pipeline dashboard export to your GitHub as code. When a rep leaves, moving their book is a prompt or a pull request, not a support ticket.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Sales Automation With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Territories and cadences change every quarter. In Emergent, each change is a prompt to code you own. No rep is billed as a seat.

fields.tab_content_1:
New demo requests go to the right rep while they are warm

A demo request from an existing HubSpot account goes to its owner. New companies are enriched with size and region. Companies with 200 or more employees go to the enterprise rep for their region, and the rest rotate across the team. HubSpot records the new owner, then Slack alerts the rep.
fields.tab_content_2:
Post-demo follow-up stops the moment a buyer replies

The recap leaves the rep's inbox on the day of the demo, and a second email follows on day 3. With no reply by day 7, the rep gets a call task in Slack. Any reply ends the sequence and is logged on the deal.
fields.tab_content_3:
Quiet deals surface before Friday's forecast call

Every morning, each open deal is checked for days since its last logged activity. A deal with no touch in 14 days is marked on the pipeline dashboard. Its owner gets a Slack message with the deal value and the last email sent. Each flagged deal needs a next step before Friday's forecast call.
fields.tab_content_4:
When a contract is 90 days from ending, renewal work starts

Contract end dates are read from HubSpot each Monday. An account that crossed into the 90-day window since the last run gets one renewal opportunity, owned by its account manager. The manager's Slack list shows every account inside the window. Each line carries the current price and any open support tickets.

fields.howto_description: The first three steps happen on a whiteboard with your sales ops lead and settle the rules. The last four connect, test and launch the app built from them.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map how a lead becomes a customer
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write routing rules in plain English
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every source that sends you leads. Put the demo form and outbound lists at the top. Note who owns each stage and where deals tend to wait. That map becomes the pipeline stages Emergent builds and the routing that feeds them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe assignment the way your sales ops lead would explain it to a new hire. Partner referrals go to the partner manager; healthcare leads go to the rep who covers clinics. Emergent turns those sentences into rules you can read and change later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what happens when a prospect misses a booked demo or goes silent after a proposal. Pick the days each email goes out and the point where a phone call replaces email. Write the templates in your reps' own voice.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the CRM your team works in, plus the Gmail or Outlook accounts reps send from. Start with one rep's inbox and one pipeline, then add the rest. Managers keep reporting from the CRM they already use.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the few signals worth interrupting a rep for, such as a close date that keeps moving or a renewal one quarter away. Decide who hears first. The owner gets the message; their manager is copied when two days pass with no update.
fields.howto_step_6_des: For one week, the app suggests an owner for each new lead while reps keep assigning by hand. Compare its picks with theirs at the end of each day. Where the two differ, fix the rule by prompting before routing goes live.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Switch on one lead source first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn routing on for the demo form and add chat leads a week later. Watch time to first touch on the dashboard. When that number drifts, change the rule behind it with a prompt. Bring in outbound lists last.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Sales Automation From New Lead to Signed Deal' and meta title 'Sales Automation Built Around Your Process | Emergent' cover the whole job, not one feature or a sibling topic. P2 (accepted, fix on rework): meta_description 'assigns every new lead and follows up until the buyer replies' and hero 'builds the lead routing and follow-ups' name two of six jobs; nothing on the page covers the 'Signed Deal' end of the H1 (quotes, contracts), the nearest is feature_5 discount approvals, while tab 4 goes past signature into renewals.

intent.evidence: Top 10 are explainers and tool lists (IBM, HubSpot glossary, Salesforce, Zendesk, betterproposals). The page gives the definition up top ('Sales automation is software that runs the repeat work of selling on rules'), the CRM vs SFA PAA, tools (FAQ 6 and the table), examples (FAQ 9 and four tabs) and a seven-step how-to specific to sales (routing rules, cadence, CRM and inboxes).

specificity.evidence: PRICING CELL OFF-CATEGORY. why_table Emergent pricing: 'Credits, no per-approver seats, no task cap'. Against Salesforce Sales Cloud ('Per user, per month by edition') and HubSpot Sales Hub ('Per seat, per month'), the seat that costs a sales team money is the rep's, not an approver's; 'per-approver seats' is approval-workflow language (catalogue row 8) and 'no task cap' answers Zapier-style task pricing that neither CRM uses. The sales variant in rules/competitors/aab.json has no pricing override, so the hub default leaks in. Library change for Divit: a sales pricing variant built on the approved claim 'the built app has no per-seat pricing', e.g. 'Credits; reps are not billed as seats'. Same class elsewhere: faq10 'runs on credits with no task cap' (answers a per-user question with a task-cap point). GENERIC: meta_title 'Built Around Your Process' could head any hub page; name the sales job instead.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens with a full sentence that says what happens: feature_1 'Demo requests and chat leads land in one table.'; feature_4 'A close date pushed twice, or a proposal with no answer after a week, sends the owner a Slack message.'; tab_content_3 'Every morning, each open deal is checked for days since its last logged activity.'; howto_step_2 'Describe assignment the way your sales ops lead would explain it to a new hire.' No keyword labels or verbless openers. (FAQ 6's empty opener is scored under faq.)

craft.evidence: TACKED-ON ', and' ENDINGS: 11 sentences in prose fields bolt a second outcome on after a comma, so the sentence ends on an afterthought, not the important word: feature_2 ', and the outcome is written to the deal record in the CRM.'; feature_3 ', and no rep spends Friday afternoon typing it in.'; tab_content_1 'The rep gets a Slack alert, and the owner is set in HubSpot.'; tab_content_3 ', and its owner gets the deal value in Slack.'; tab_content_4 'The list posts to Slack on Monday, and a renewal opportunity opens in the CRM for each account.'; faq3 'Most CRMs include some of it, and teams that need more add a layer on top.'; faq4 ', and it runs on any CRM, HubSpot and Pipedrive included.'; faq5 ', and managers get a forecast built from the deals that are open today.'; faq8 'A form fill starts a nurture sequence, and a reply books a meeting.'; faq10 ', and it is free to start.'; howto_step_5 ', and it repeats daily until someone acts on it.' Three of four tab paragraphs end this way. Split them or restructure so each sentence carries one idea and ends on it; keep at most two on the page. (tab_content_1 'and the rest rotate across the team' and tab_content_2 'and another email follows on day 3' are real sequences and can stay.)

voice.evidence: HEDGE OPENER: faq6 'It depends on where the gap is.' (a machine tell; answer the question first). SAME IDEA TOLD TWICE: features_subheading 'Sales automation is software that runs the repeat work of selling on rules, while reps keep the conversations.' and faq1 'Sales automation is software that handles the admin of selling... Reps keep the work that needs judgment' (same definition, same opener, same 'reps keep' turn); feature_4 'The reminder repeats each morning until someone updates the deal.' and howto_step_5 'it repeats daily until someone acts on it'; howto_description 'Emergent turns those rules into a working app' and howto_step_2 'Emergent turns those sentences into rules'; faq5 'It logs each email and meeting against the deal' restates feature_3 'Sent emails and meeting notes sync to Salesforce or HubSpot'. Each repeated idea should appear once, the second place should add something new (catalogue row 18).

truth.evidence: 1) why_table Emergent pricing 'no per-approver seats, no task cap': not meaningful against per-user CRMs (see specificity); Salesforce and HubSpot do not sell by task, so 'no task cap' implies a limit they do not have (catalogue row 8 class). 2) faq4 'No. Salesforce automation means the flows and rules configured inside Salesforce' is stated as settled; 'salesforce automation' is widely used as a spelling of sales force automation (the term predates the company). Answer that it can mean either, then separate them. 3) howto_step_7 'every version of the workflow is saved in your repo' states platform behaviour as automatic (catalogue row 14); the approved claim is code export to GitHub, so write it as something the team does ('push each version to your repo'). 4) tab_content_4 H3 'Start every renewal 90 days before the contract ends' vs the image: the 'Renewal opportunity created' mini is for Hooli at '21 days', which means the opportunity was not started at 90 days; and 'a renewal opportunity opens in the CRM for each account' on a weekly list would reopen duplicates every Monday (also in mockup renewalReminders 'create a renewal opportunity for each account'). Say it opens when an account enters the 90-day window, and draw it for Northwind at 85 days. 5) Cross-tab cast contradicts the copy: Globex is a new inbound demo request routed to M. Rossi (uc-1, cover 'New lead: Globex'), an open $52,000 Evaluation deal (uc-3), and an existing customer at '$64,000 a year' renewing in 63 days under Priya Shah (uc-4). tab_content_1 says each request is 'checked against the CRM for an existing account' and howto_step_2 says 'Named accounts stay with their current owner', so an existing customer cannot land as a new lead with a new owner. Hooli (new 2,400-employee lead in uc-1, '$42,000 a year' customer in uc-4) and Northwind (Proposal deal in uc-3, customer in uc-4) repeat the problem. 6) uc-2: hero line 'Recap opened twice, last on Oct 10' while the timeline says 'Second email, Day 3, opened twice' and shows no opens on the recap. 7) faq8 'a reply books a meeting': a reply does not book anything; say a reply ends the sequence or sends a booking link.

distinct.evidence: Nouns swapped from the AP and approval-workflow siblings: howto_step_6 'Run a quarter of real leads and deals through the workflow before go-live... adjust any rule that disagrees by prompting, and replay it until the two lists match.' vs AP howto_step_6 'Run last month's invoices through the automated AP workflow before go-live... fix the rule by prompting and run the sample again until the two match.'; howto_step_7 'every version of the workflow is saved in your repo' vs AP step 7 'Every rule change is versioned in your repo' vs approval-workflow step 7 'with every version kept in exportable code'; why_description 'Sales platforms price by seat and keep your playbook in their app.' vs approval-workflow 'Most approval tools charge per user and keep the audit trail in their app.' and AP 'your approval rules live inside the vendor's app'; feature_6 'Routing rules and sequences export to your GitHub repository... hand the code to one of your engineers' vs AP feature_6 'The matching rules and the approval chain export to your GitHub repository as code your engineers can review.' Write a sales-specific dry run (e.g. a shadow week where the app suggests owners and reps accept or reassign) and a sales-specific go-live and why line.

faq.evidence: Exactly 10 on-topic items, hub link in item 2, sibling links to crm-automation, lead-nurturing-workflow and approval-workflow read naturally. Fails: faq6 'What are the best sales automation tools?' opens 'It depends on where the gap is.', not an answer in the first sentence; faq10 'How much does sales automation software cost?' never gives a cost or range and ends on 'no task cap', which does not apply to per-user CRMs; faq1 restates features_subheading (same definition); faq5 restates feature_3 (emails and meetings logged to the deal); faq4 opens with a flat 'No.' that is contestable (see truth).

images.evidence: 1) Third-party fictional IP (docs/IMAGE_BRIEF.md rule 6 lists neutral placeholders): 'Umbrella Co' (uc-3 table row, hero 'Umbrella Co quiet for 19 days', alt) is Capcom's Resident Evil villain corporation, a live trademark sold as merchandise; 'Hooli' (uc-1 table, uc-4 list, hero 'Hooli renews in 21 days', mini 'Hooli, in HubSpot', alt) is HBO's Silicon Valley; 'Stark Labs' (uc-1 table) leans on Marvel's Stark Industries and DC's S.T.A.R. Labs; 'Vandelay' (uc-1 table) is the Seinfeld gag. Replace all four with neutral invented names. Globex, Initech, Acme Corp and Northwind are the brief's own list and can stay. 2) uc-4 opportunity drawn for Hooli at 21 days against the H3 'Start every renewal 90 days before the contract ends' (see truth 4). 3) Same companies in incompatible roles across tabs: Globex new lead (uc-1, cover) vs $64,000-a-year customer (uc-4); Hooli new lead (uc-1) vs customer (uc-4); Northwind open deal (uc-3) vs customer (uc-4). 4) uc-2 'Recap opened twice' (hero) vs 'Second email, Day 3, opened twice' (timeline). 5) P2: owner names mix formats in one column, uc-3 'J. Alvarez', 'M. Rossi', 'Dana Ruiz'; 'Priya' is the healthcare rep in howto_step_2 and the account manager 'Priya Shah' in uc-4. Layout itself is good: one hero per panel, readable text, cursor on button edges, uc-1 routing and uc-3 counts add up.

claims_to_source: Sales force automation (SFA) is the long-standing category name for software that automates a sales team's lead, account and opportunity work; it is not the name of one vendor
SFA is a subset of CRM: a CRM holds the customer record, SFA automates the sales activity on it
Salesforce Flow is Salesforce's tool for automating processes inside the Salesforce CRM
Pipedrive and HubSpot both include workflow automation (trigger and action) inside the CRM
HubSpot sequences can end a contact's enrollment when the contact replies or books a meeting
HubSpot workflows can rotate new records across a set of owners (round robin)
Outreach is a sales engagement platform built around sequences and calling
Sales automation covers rule-based steps such as lead routing, follow-up email, CRM updates and pipeline reminders
Flagging deals with no logged activity in 14 days is a common pipeline-hygiene rule
Renewal work commonly starts 90 days or more before a contract ends
Sales CRMs and engagement platforms price per user or seat per month, with automation in higher editions
